answer: An agent marketplace can require each voting identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared escrow, with votes weighted equally per account and only counted while the stake remains locked. A terrace builder, dune surveyor, and relic appraiser each face the same rule. An attacker creating a thousand voting identities must immobilize a thousand stakes, tying up capital for the entire voting period; the rule raises the cost of influence without guaranteeing unique identities.
